question: Which Linux notification backend contract should OpenClaw support for headless node hosts: `notify-send` only, broader D-Bus/`dunstify` fallback support, or deferral to a native Linux companion app?
rationale: The code path is clear, but backend dependencies, fallback behavior, and safe handling of desktop-session availability are product/security choices that automation should not settle alone.

options.title: Start with notify-send only
options.body: Implement a focused `notify-send` path with no shell, desktop-session detection, documented dependency expectations, and structured unavailable errors.

options.title: Support multiple backends now
options.body: Add `notify-send` plus D-Bus or `dunstify` fallbacks, accepting a larger support and security-review surface for better desktop coverage.

options.title: Defer to native Linux app
options.body: Leave headless Linux `system.notify` unsupported until Linux companion-app ownership defines native notification behavior.

recommendation.title: Start with notify-send only
recommendation.body: Implement a focused `notify-send` path with no shell, desktop-session detection, documented dependency expectations, and structured unavailable errors.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest current history across the node-host, CLI, docs, policy, and reserved-command surfaces involved in the decision.
